fx_note: Approximate exchange rates (1 EUR in local currency), only used to convert caps and thresholds in the comparison tool.

locations.name: United Kingdom

film_uplift.label: Independent Film Tax Credit (53%, 39.75% net) for films with a core budget up to £23.5m, paid on the first £15m of core expenditure

locations.min_spend: At least 10% of core spend in the UK; high-end TV at least £1m per broadcast hour
locations.cap_label: No cap; qualifying spend limited to 80% of core expenditure
locations.funding_note: Statutory credit, no annual budget
locations.paid: After the corporation tax return
locations.notes: The credit is taxable, so 34% is worth 25.5% net. 39% for animation, children's TV and UK VFX work (VFX is exempt from the 80% cap). 53% for independent films with a core budget up to £23.5m, on the first £15m of spend. Qualifying spend is limited to 80% of core expenditure. The old film and HETV reliefs close on 1 April 2027.

budget_template.label: AVEC stencil (Excel), BFI
budget_template.note: A calculation sheet for the claim, giving HMRC the expenditure statement it needs. Not a budgeting format: budget in your own layout and split UK and non-UK core expenditure.

locations.name: Ireland

film_uplift.label: Scéal uplift (40%) for feature films with eligible expenditure under €20m and an Irish or EEA key creative

locations.min_spend: €125k eligible spend and €250k total production cost
locations.funding_note: Payable credit, no annual budget; up to 90% can be claimed in advance
locations.paid: Up to 90% in advance, balance on completion
locations.notes: Credit is paid untaxed. 40% for feature films with eligible spend under €20m (Scéal) and 40% on the first €10m of VFX spend when at least €1m goes to Irish VFX. Cast and crew of any nationality qualify when working in Ireland. Runs to end 2028.

budget_template.label: Section 481 guidance, Screen Ireland
budget_template.note: No prescribed budget format. Revenue's application takes your own detailed budget and finance plan; Screen Ireland's page lists the compliance documents that go with it.

locations.name: Netherlands
locations.min_spend: Feature: €1m total cost and €150k Dutch spend; documentary: €250k and €100k; high-end series: €12,000 per broadcast minute for drama (€8,000 animation, €4,000 documentary) and at least €1m per episode

cap.label: €3m per project and per company per year

locations.funding_note: Competitive rounds, ranked on points: €20m for film in four rounds and €9.5m for high-end series in three rounds in 2026, with international co-productions served first up to 70% of a round
locations.paid: In instalments under the implementation agreement; the final amount is set on the audited qualifying spend
locations.notes: Selective: applications are ranked, so a strong project can still miss out when a round is oversubscribed. A Dutch producer or co-producer is required. International co-productions are served first in 2026. Next deadline for film and series: 26 October 2026.

budget_template.label: Budget model Standard & Production Incentive (Excel), Netherlands Film Fund
budget_template.note: Mandatory format. Also published as a Movie Magic template and an animation version on the same downloads list.

locations.name: Belgium
locations.assumption: No statutory rate: 38% is the typical net benefit of investor financing after the investor return and fees
locations.min_spend: No statutory minimum; tax shelter money limited to 50% of the budget
locations.funding_note: Depends on investor appetite via intermediaries, no state budget
locations.paid: Up front: it is financing, not a rebate
locations.notes: Not a rebate but private financing with a tax break for the investor. The producer's net benefit is typically 38 to 40% of eligible Belgian spend. Money arrives before the shoot. Requires a Belgian (co-)producer and a European work.

budget_template.label: Project budget Screen Flanders / VAF 2026 (Excel)
budget_template.note: The tax shelter itself has no prescribed budget format: the intermediary and FPS Finance work from your own budget. Flemish co-producers use this joint form for their Screen Flanders and VAF applications; Wallonia has its own forms.

locations.name: Germany
locations.min_spend: DFFF I: €1m total cost (€200k documentary, €2m animation) and 25% German spend (20% above €20m); DFFF II: €20m budget and €8m German spend; GMPF series: €30k per minute

cap.label: €5m (DFFF I) to €25m (DFFF II) per project; series up to €20m per season

locations.funding_note: First come, first served; the €250m for DFFF I, DFFF II and GMPF in 2026 was fully committed by 20 August 2026
locations.paid: Four instalments of 25%: start of shoot, mid-production, rough cut, final audit
locations.notes: 30% since February 2025 across all three schemes. The federal pot was doubled to €250m for 2026 and ran out on 20 August 2026; the window for shoots starting in 2027 opens in November 2026. Public aid is capped at 50% of the total cost.

budget_template.label: DFFF calculation scheme for feature and documentary films (Excel), FFA
budget_template.note: Optional layout: the FFA also accepts Sesam, Movie Magic and PreProducer budgets, as long as the German costs are identifiable.

locations.name: France
locations.scheme: Tax Rebate for International Production (TRIP / C2I)
locations.min_spend: €250k French spend (or 50% of the budget when the budget is under €500k) and 5 shooting days in France for live action
locations.funding_note: Statutory credit, no annual budget
locations.paid: After the fiscal year, via the French line producer
locations.notes: 40% when at least 15% of the shots are digitally treated and French VFX spend exceeds €2m. The 2026 finance law adds the pay of non-European performers hired by the French executive producer to the eligible base and extends the scheme to end 2028. Paid via the French line producer after the tax year, so budget for interim financing.

budget_template.label: Provisional approval application form for fiction (Excel), CNC
budget_template.note: Mandatory form for the agrément provisoire, filed by the French executive producer with the breakdown of French expenditure. Separate versions for animation and VFX works on the CNC page.

locations.name: Spain (mainland)
locations.min_spend: €1m Spanish spend (€200k for animation and post)
locations.funding_note: Statutory deduction, no annual budget
locations.paid: Through the tax position of a Spanish service company
locations.notes: 30% on the first €1m of Spanish spend, 25% above that. Claimed by an ICAA-registered Spanish service company and passed on through the service contract. Regional schemes go higher: Navarre 35%, Bizkaia up to 60%.

budget_template.label: Cultural certificate for foreign shoots, ICAA
budget_template.note: No prescribed budget format. The Spanish service company applies for the ICAA cultural certificate with the official technical and artistic sheet plus its own budget, then claims the deduction in its tax return.

locations.name: Canary Islands (Spain)
locations.min_spend: €1m Canary Islands spend (€200k for animation and post)
locations.funding_note: Statutory deduction, no annual budget
locations.paid: Through the tax position of a Canary Islands service company
locations.notes: 50% on the first €1m, 45% above that (54% on the first €1m when Canary spend exceeds €1.8m). Requires a production or service company resident in the Canary Islands and a regional certificate.

budget_template.label: List of qualifying expenditure (PDF), Tenerife Film Commission
budget_template.note: No budget format is prescribed; this list shows which cost lines count as Canary spend. The ICAA cultural certificate and the Canary Islands certificate go with the claim.

locations.name: Italy
locations.min_spend: €250k Italian spend

cap.label: €20m per company or group per year; no per-project cap

locations.funding_note: Closed annual budget since 2026: the 2026 window ran from 3 June to 31 August 2026 (decree of 19 May 2026), and requests beyond the available resources roll into a later session if funds allow
locations.paid: Offset against Italian tax or sold to a bank at a 5 to 15% discount; 70% of an approved provisional credit can be used at once
locations.notes: Transferable credit granted to the Italian executive producer. Since the 2024 revision: €20m per company per year, AI-related costs excluded, above-the-line costs of non-EEA persons at 30%. In 2026 Italy added caps per work and per company and a closed annual budget with fixed application windows, after revoking €66m of credits in 2025.

budget_template.label: Tax credit notices and application windows, DGCA
budget_template.note: No public template. The Italian executive producer files the cost plan on the DGCOL platform; the final request needs the eligible costs certified by an auditor registered there.

locations.name: Portugal
locations.min_spend: €2.5m eligible spend (large track); €500k (medium track, €200k for documentaries and non-filming activities)

cap.label: €6m per work and €3m per episode (large track); €1m (medium track)

locations.funding_note: First come, first served; €35m a year for the large track and €15m for the medium track, 2026 to 2029
locations.paid: Large track: after completion, by the end of April of the following year; medium track: four instalments from contract signature
locations.notes: New scheme since June 2026, replacing the old cash rebate. Large track: 30% on the first €2m, 25% above (30% throughout in the interior, Madeira and the Azores). Medium track: 30%, or 40% in those regions. Cultural test and a local executive producer required.

budget_template.label: Eligible expenditure budget (Excel), Portugal Film Commission
budget_template.note: Mandatory attachment to the SCRI.PT application, alongside the cultural self-assessment grid.

locations.name: Malta
locations.assumption: Assumes the full 40%: 30% base, 35% with Maltese content or Malta Film Studios, 40% when local crew targets are met
locations.min_spend: €100k Malta spend and a budget above €200k
locations.cap_label: No per-project cap; rebate on above-the-line costs capped at €1m or 30% of Malta spend, up to €5m; eligible spend limited to 80% of the budget
locations.funding_note: No published annual budget
locations.paid: 10% advance, balance after final audit
locations.notes: 30% base, 35% when Malta plays Malta or Malta Film Studios are used, 40% when local crew and department targets are met. Crew of any nationality qualifies. Scheme valid to October 2028.

budget_template.label: Financial incentives guidelines June 2024 (PDF), Screen Malta
budget_template.note: No template. The application takes a top sheet of the overall budget plus an itemised estimate of the Malta spend, with the Financial Form and cultural test from these guidelines.

locations.name: Hungary
locations.min_spend: No published minimum; cultural test
locations.cap_label: No per-project cap; annual envelope HUF 70bn (2026)
locations.funding_note: Annual collection account of HUF 70bn. The HUF 140bn cap for new registrations in the first half of 2026 expired and registration reopened without a cap on 1 July 2026, with a backlog of several months
locations.paid: After audit, in HUF
locations.notes: Non-Hungarian costs may make up to 25% of the eligible spend, which lifts the effective rebate to 37.5% of Hungarian spend. Principal photography must start within 6 months of registration, applied for at least 30 days before the shoot. Paid in forint, so budget the currency risk; the NFI charges up to 2.5% administration.

budget_template.label: Registration procedure and forms, National Film Office
budget_template.note: No downloadable Excel: the budget goes into the Film Office's form-filling application, with cost lines fixed by the decree annex. Hungarian language.

locations.name: Czech Republic
locations.min_spend: CZK 18m feature film, CZK 7.5m per series episode, CZK 5m animated film, CZK 2.5m documentary; digital productions CZK 5m flat
locations.funding_note: Annual budget; registration was halted on 27 March 2026 and reopened on 1 September 2026
locations.paid: After completion, in CZK; since 2026 the registration decision no longer states the amount and payment can take up to 2 years
locations.notes: 25% since 2025 (up from 20%), 35% for animation and VFX-only projects, plus 66% of the withholding tax paid by foreign cast and crew. Public aid is capped at 50% of the budget and claims must be filed within 3 years of registration.

budget_template.label: Registration forms 2026 (ZIP, Czech), Czech Audiovisual Fund
budget_template.note: Mandatory forms including the budget and cost tables, in Czech; the fund's applicant guide explains them. The rebate is paid on the audited actual costs.

locations.name: Poland
locations.min_spend: Eligible Polish spend of at least PLN 4m for a co-produced feature (PLN 1m for a service production), PLN 1m per drama series episode and PLN 300k for a documentary; 75% of the financing secured; cultural test

cap.label: PLN 15m per production, PLN 20m per beneficiary per year

locations.funding_note: First come, first served until the annual pot is used
locations.paid: After the final report is verified, in PLN
locations.notes: Rolling applications until the annual budget is exhausted, with at least 10% reserved for animation. Requires a Polish producer, co-producer or service company; applications are in Polish. Eligible costs are limited to 80% of the budget and public aid to 50%.

budget_template.label: Incentive information and application system, Polish Film Institute
budget_template.note: Applications go through the PISF online system in Polish, with the cost estimate as an attachment; PISF publishes a macro-enabled Excel cost estimate for its funding programmes.

locations.name: Iceland

spend_uplift.label: 35% when Icelandic spend is at least ISK 350m with at least 30 working days and 50 crew in Iceland

locations.min_spend: None
locations.funding_note: Open-ended, no annual budget
locations.paid: After completion and audit, in ISK
locations.notes: 35% when the production spends at least ISK 350m in Iceland over 30+ working days with 50+ crew, and for content made for audiences under 18. If more than 80% of the total cost is incurred in Iceland, costs elsewhere in the EEA also qualify. Extended to end 2028.

budget_template.label: Guidelines for the letter of intent (PDF), Icelandic Film Centre
budget_template.note: No template: the application takes an itemised budget and financing plan in your own format. These guidelines list the attachments; a second guide covers the payment application.

locations.name: Norway
locations.assumption: Assumes the project is selected; only five projects were funded in 2026
locations.min_spend: NOK 25m feature budget or NOK 10m per drama series episode (NOK 10m for a documentary feature, NOK 5m per documentary series episode); at least NOK 4m Norwegian spend and 30% non-Norwegian financing
locations.cap_label: Set per project by the annual award (NOK 84.7m across five projects in 2026: one feature and four drama series)
locations.funding_note: One competitive round a year, heavily oversubscribed; the 2027 round is expected to open in June with a deadline in November
locations.paid: After completion, in NOK
locations.notes: Ranked selection against a small annual envelope: 18 applicants asked for NOK 288m in 2026 and five were funded. Requires a Norwegian company or a branch of an EEA or UK company. Parliament has asked for a more competitive scheme from 2027.

budget_template.label: Application requirements, Norwegian Film Institute
budget_template.note: No template: the NFI portal asks for the total production budget and a separate budget for the Norwegian spend in your own format, plus an auditor's statement on the NFI template at the end.

locations.name: Austria
locations.min_spend: €150k eligible Austrian costs for a fiction feature or series; €80k for documentary or VR

cap.label: €5m per film or single episode, €7.5m per series or season

locations.funding_note: No legal entitlement: first come, first served against federal funds. Intake for 2026 reopened on 2 January 2026 and processing takes about six weeks; the 2026 total budget is not published.
locations.paid: In three instalments: 30% at the start of the Austrian shoot, 40% after Austrian shooting wraps, 30% after final audit
locations.notes: A non-repayable grant, not a tax credit. Base rate is up to 30% of eligible costs (the assessment base is itself capped at 80% of total production cost). A Green Bonus for sustainable production adds up to 5 points, and a separate flat EUR 25,000 bonus is available for meeting female head-of-department targets. Fees paid to foreign cast or crew under Austrian withholding tax count for only 50% of the Austria-taxable amount. Current guidelines run from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027.

budget_template.label: FISA+ processing document 2026 (Excel)
budget_template.note: Mandatory workbook with the cost calculation, filed through the aws Fördermanager; the same file is used for the final settlement. German language, about 7 MB.

locations.name: Croatia
locations.scheme: Filming in Croatia Production Incentive Programme
locations.min_spend: €250k feature film, €150k TV film, €100k per TV series episode, €60k for documentary, animation or a post-production-only application
locations.cap_label: No per-project cap stated; the aid, together with other state aid, may not exceed 50% of the budget
locations.funding_note: Awarded on a first-come, first-served basis. The current annual state budget for the scheme and its open or closed status are not published on the official sites.
locations.paid: After completion: a Provisional Certificate is issued on qualification, and payment follows a Final Certificate once the audited accounts of the Croatian shoot are approved
locations.notes: At least 30% of cast and crew working in Croatia must be Croatian or EEA citizens for a partial shoot, 50% for a full shoot; above €500k of incentive one Croatian trainee per main department, above €1m three Croatian heads of department and 50% Croatian tax residents in the crew. Only spend inside Croatia and wages of Croatian tax residents qualify, capped at 80% of the budget. 70% of the Croatian financing must be secured at application.

budget_template.label: Service production application forms (ZIP, Croatian), HAVC
budget_template.note: Mandatory forms including the budget of the Croatian spend, in Croatian. A separate package exists for co-productions.

locations.name: Denmark
locations.min_spend: DKK 3m Danish spend for a feature film or fiction series (DKK 1m for documentary); minimum total budget DKK 25m for a feature film, DKK 150k per minute and DKK 15m per season for a fiction series, DKK 4m for documentary
locations.funding_note: DKK 100m a year for live action and DKK 25m for animation, in two rounds; DKK 58m was open in the September 2026 round. Applications are ranked on Danish spend, total budget and the production and cultural test, so a qualifying project can still miss out
locations.paid: 70% once the auditor-endorsed financing plan is in, 30% after the final report is approved
locations.notes: New since 1 January 2026. At least 60% of the financing must be confirmed at application and at least 25% must come from foreign sources; the lead producer needs a prior credit with wide distribution. Deadline 24 September 2026, next round expected 8 April 2027. Regional funds such as Copenhagen Film Fund and FilmFyn still operate alongside as discretionary co-investors.
locations.source_label: Slots- og Kulturstyrelsen (Danish Agency for Culture and Palaces)

budget_template.label: Total budget and eligible expenditure (Excel), Danish Agency for Culture and Palaces
budget_template.note: Mandatory template, with a matching financing plan template and the test workbook on the scheme page.

locations.name: Finland
locations.min_spend: €500k Finnish spend; minimum total budget €2.5m for a feature film, €650k for a documentary and €11,500 per minute for series and animation; at least 25% foreign financing
locations.cap_label: No per-project cap stated; eligible Finnish spend is itself capped at 80% of the total production budget
locations.funding_note: Rolling applications against an annual budget under a decree covering 2024 to 2026. The 2026 budget is €10m, with about €7m still available in September 2026; renewal beyond 2026 is not confirmed.
locations.paid: After completion only, based on audited costs; no advance payment
locations.notes: Administered by Business Finland. Only costs from Finland-tax-liable companies and wages subject to Finnish withholding tax qualify; nationality-neutral. A foreign applicant files through a Finnish production coordinator. Terms effective 1 January 2026.

budget_template.label: Cost breakdown, Finnish part (Excel), Business Finland
budget_template.note: Mandatory attachment to the application; the same breakdown is used for the final cost report.

locations.name: Greece
locations.min_spend: €200k for a feature film or TV fiction (varies by category: €60k documentary, €45k short film, €120k per episode for a mini-series up to 16 episodes, €35k per episode for other fiction series, €80k animated feature, €50k animated short)

cap.label: €8m per work (up to €10m for strategic projects by ministerial decision)

locations.funding_note: €100m for 2026 (€88m film and TV, €10m animation, €2m games); applications opened 28 April 2026 on the state OPSKE platform and are served until the envelope is used
locations.paid: After completion and audit, within 3 months of the completion certification decision
locations.notes: Administered by the Hellenic Film and Audiovisual Center, Creative Greece (formerly EKOME). Eligible expenses are capped at 80% of the total budget and must be incurred in Greece, except one director's fee and up to two lead actors' fees on foreign invoices. A separate 30% tax relief exists for investors.
locations.source_label: Hellenic Film and Audiovisual Center, Creative Greece (formerly EKOME)

budget_template.label: CRGR scheme page, Creative Greece
budget_template.note: No public template: the application and its cost table are entered on the OPSKE platform (ependyseis.gr) by the Greek production company, at least 10 days before the shoot.

locations.name: Sweden
locations.min_spend: SEK 4m eligible Swedish costs; minimum total budget SEK 30m for a feature film, SEK 10m for a documentary film, SEK 10m per episode for a drama series, SEK 5m per episode for a documentary series
locations.funding_note: SEK 82.5m in the 2026 round (applications 25 August to 8 September 2026); productions with the highest eligible costs are prioritised, so a qualifying project can still miss out
locations.paid: After completion, claimed within 3 months
locations.notes: In force since 20 September 2022. Only costs from Sweden-tax-liable businesses or workers qualify, and the production must pass a cultural test. Administration is set to move from Tillväxtverket to the Swedish Film Institute from 1 January 2027. Regional funds such as Film i Väst, Filmpool Nord and Film i Skåne operate alongside as discretionary co-investors.
locations.source_label: Tillväxtverket (Swedish Agency for Economic and Regional Growth)

budget_template.label: Application form and templates, Tillväxtverket
budget_template.note: No budget template: attach an itemised budget for the whole production, for example from Movie Magic, as PDF or Excel, plus the production description template.

labour_note: Share of local spend assumed to be local labour, for schemes that only credit labour (Canada). Adjustable.
scope_note: Europe only for now (no Russia or Belarus). Entries for Canada, the US, Australia, New Zealand and South Africa are kept in git history (commit e0dfd82) until we decide to show them.
